title: Visualise Sports Injuries With Anatomical Heatmaps
text: Start creating data frame: run injury_heatmap(injury_data, selected_sport, view_choice) : injury_data: data used, .e. data frame selected_sport: column name use view_choice: view diagram. One : "front", "back", "" Run ?injury_heatmap detail.
code: Subcategory <- c("Head","Neck","Shoulder","Chest","Upper Arm","Elbow",                  "Abdomen","Forearm","Hip Groin","Wrist","Hand",                  "Thigh","Knee","Lower Leg","Ankle","Foot","Thoracic Spine","Lumbosacral")  Region.area <- rep("Example", length(Subcategory)) boxing <- c(15, 5, 18, 12, 20, 6, 10, 14, 9, 9, 11, 3, 16, 13, 7, 8, 18, 22)  df <- data.frame(Region.area, Subcategory, boxing) injury_heatmap(df, "boxing", "front", sex = "male", show_scale = FALSE)

title: Heat map of Injuries on Human Body — injury_heatmap
text: injury_data data frame body region, area injury occurred, frequency injury selected_sport name sport, corresponding header frequency column data frame. view_choice view render diagram. One ("front", "back", "") sex body diagram use: "male" "female". palette Optional colour palette. single palette name supported diagram_colours (viridis HCL), e.g. "magma" "Reds". character vector hex colours, e.g. c("#FFFFFF", "#FF0000"). HCL palette names can listed grDevices::hcl.pals(). opacity Numeric 0 1. Opacity filled body regions. show_labels Logical. TRUE, show region names. show_values Logical. TRUE, show injury values. show_scale Logical. TRUE, show colour scale (legend).

title: Heat map of Injuries on Human Body — injury_heatmap
code: Subcategory <- c("Head","Neck","Shoulder","Chest","Upper Arm","Elbow",                   "Abdomen","Forearm","Hip Groin","Wrist","Hand",                   "Thigh","Knee","Lower Leg","Ankle","Foot","Thoracic Spine","Lumbosacral") Region.area <- rep("Example", length(Subcategory)) boxing <- c(15, 5, 18, 12, 20, 6, 10, 14, 9, 9, 11, 3, 16, 13, 7, 8, 18, 22) df <- data.frame(Region.area, Subcategory, boxing) # Generate a plot for front view, male p1 <- injury_heatmap(df, "boxing", "front", sex = "male", show_values = FALSE) #> Error in loadNamespace(x): there is no package called ‘rsvg’ # You can customise the colour palette by: p2 <- injury_heatmap(df, "boxing", "front", sex = "female", palette = "plasma") #> Error in loadNamespace(x): there is no package called ‘rsvg’ # You can add your own plot title by: p2 + ggplot2::labs(title = "Boxing Injury Heatmap (Front)") #> Error: object 'p2' not found

title: Test colour palette(s) — test_colour
code: # values from hcl.pals() test_colour("Greens")  test_colour(list("Reds","Blues"))  # values from viridis, localised to color test_colour("Grays")   # Custom colour palette custom_palette <- c("#cba6f7", "#f38ba8", "#eba0ac", "#f9e2af", "#fab387", "#a6e3a1", "#94e2d5", "#74c7ec", "#89b4fa", "#b4befe") test_colour(custom_palette)   # Multiple custom and existing palettes custom_palette <- c("#cba6f7", "#f38ba8", "#eba0ac", "#f9e2af", "#fab387", "#a6e3a1", "#94e2d5", "#74c7ec", "#89b4fa", "#b4befe") custom_palette_2 <- c("#8839ef", "#d20f39", "#e64553", "#df8e1d", "#fe640b", "#40a02b", "#179299", "#209fb5", "#1e66f5", "#7287fd") test_colour(list(custom_palette,"Blues", "Greens", custom_palette_2))  # All hcl colours test_colour(hcl.pals())                                                                                                                    # All colourblind palettes viridis_palettes <- list("magma", "inferno", "plasma", "viridis", "cividis",  "rocket", "mako", "turbo")

title: spinviz 0.0.1.0000
text: Removed duplicate grDevices entry DESCRIPTION Imports. Added tests/testthat suite covering diagram_colours(), test_colour(), injury_heatmap(). injury_heatmap() longer calls print() result returning , previously caused plot render twice R Markdown/Quarto documents call left unassigned. injury_heatmap() now warns values selected sport column converted numeric, instead silently coercing NA. injury_heatmap()’s documentation palette argument now regenerated longer shows stale “WIP” placeholder text. injury_heatmap()’s front/back label coordinate tables now built single shared lookup (label_position_lookup()) instead two hand-duplicated tables, views silently drift apart. injury_heatmap()’s combined “views” label table (both_label_position_lookup()) now validates front-/back-regions single source truth (view_exclusive_regions()) used SVG id per-view label lookups, instead re-encoding regions one-sided third time. test_colour() now restores caller’s graphics::par() settings exit instead permanently changing plotting layout (mfrow). Fixed documentation typo test_colour() (“coloublind” -> “colourblind”).
